title: Gluten-Free Corn Seasoning Recipes for Summer Grilling
meta_description: Level up your BBQ with these easy gluten free corn seasoning recipes. Plus, keep your hands clean with the best interlocking corn cob holders.
html:
There is nothing quite like the smell of corn roasting over an open flame in July. But if you’re cooking for a crowd with dietary restrictions, you know that the danger often lies in the rubs and pre-made seasonings. Many store-bought corn seasonings use wheat-based fillers or soy sauce containing gluten, which can ruin a great meal for sensitive guests.

The good news is that creating a delicious gluten free corn seasoning is incredibly simple. Most of the best flavors come from fresh herbs, citrus, and spices that are naturally gluten-free. Whether you prefer a smoky BBQ vibe, a zesty Mexican street corn style, or something sweet and buttery, these recipes will keep your grill game strong all summer long.

Zesty Garlic Herb Butter (The Classic)

You can't go wrong with a garlic-herb blend. The key here is using high-quality salted butter and fresh herbs. This blend works perfectly whether you grill your corn in the husk or strip it down for those charred, caramelized kernels.

Melt half a cup of unsalted butter and stir in three cloves of minced garlic, a tablespoon of chopped fresh parsley, and a teaspoon of dried oregano. Add a pinch of sea salt and cracked black pepper. Brush this on halfway through grilling and again right before serving.

Since this butter is rich and slippery, this is the perfect time to bring out the Interlocking Corn on the Cob Holders (5 Pairs). They keep your fingers away from the melted butter and the hot grill, and the silicone handles make them easy to grip even when your hands are a bit greasy.

Mexican Street Corn (Elote) Gluten Free Corn Seasoning

Traditional Elote is a crowd favorite, but some pre-mixed chili powders contain anti-caking agents that aren't gluten-free. Making your own ensures your guests stay safe while enjoying those bold, creamy flavors.

For this version, you'll need:

  • 1/4 cup Mayonnaise (check label for GF certification)
  • 1/4 cup Sour cream or Mexican Crema
  • 1/2 tsp Smoked paprika
  • 1/2 tsp Chili powder
  • 1/4 cup crumbled Cotija cheese
  • Fresh lime wedges and cilantro for garnish

Mix the mayo, sour cream, and spices together. Slather the mixture over grilled corn, roll the cob in Cotija cheese, and finish with a heavy squeeze of lime. It's a flavor bomb that proves you don't need wheat-based additives to get a professional taste.

Sweet and Smoky BBQ Rub

If you want a dry rub rather than a wet butter, a smoky BBQ blend is the way to go. Dry rubs create a beautiful crust on the corn that tastes like a professional smokehouse. Just be sure to avoid pre-made BBQ rubs that list "malt vinegar" or "barley" as ingredients.

Combine brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and a hint of cayenne pepper. Rub a small amount of oil on the corn first so the seasoning sticks, then coat generously with the rub. Grill over medium heat, turning frequently to prevent the sugar from burning.

Once these are off the grill, serving them can be messy. Using the Interlocking Corn on the Cob Holders (5 Pairs) makes the plating process much tidier, and since they are dishwasher safe, you don't have to worry about the sticky BBQ residue lingering on the tools.

Honey Sriracha Glaze for a Spicy Kick

For those who like a bit of heat, a honey-Sriracha glaze is an excellent gluten free corn seasoning choice. Most Sriracha brands are gluten-free, but always double-check the label for hidden thickeners.

Whisk together two tablespoons of honey, one tablespoon of Sriracha, and a tablespoon of melted butter. Brush this glaze onto the corn during the last three minutes of grilling. The honey caramelizes under the heat, creating a sticky, spicy-sweet coating that pairs perfectly with grilled shrimp or burgers.

Tips for the Perfect Grilled Corn

To get the most out of your seasonings, timing is everything. For butter-based mixtures, apply them in layers. A light coat at the start helps the corn cook, and a fresh coat at the end provides the punch of flavor.

If you are grilling in the husk, soak the corn in water for 15 minutes first. This prevents the husks from burning too quickly and steams the kernels inside. Once removed from the husk, apply your chosen gluten free corn seasoning immediately while the kernels are still steaming and open to absorbing flavor.

Finally, organization is key for a stress-free BBQ. The interlocking design of the Interlocking Corn on the Cob Holders (5 Pairs) means they won't roll around in your kitchen drawer or get lost in the grill tool set, making them the ideal party-ready accessory.

FAQ

Is corn naturally gluten-free?

Yes, corn is naturally gluten-free. However, the risk comes from processed seasonings, cross-contamination in the kitchen, or butter blends that include wheat-based stabilizers.

Can I make these seasonings ahead of time?

Absolutely. Dry rubs can be made weeks in advance and stored in airtight containers. Butter-based blends can be made 2-3 days ahead and kept in the refrigerator; just let them soften or gently reheat them before brushing onto the corn.

How do I clean silicone corn holders?
